title: T-3364: 2009 Prairie's elliptical-arched entrance, carved course over the door and oriel frieze
body:
## T-3364: 2009 Prairie's entrance, the carved course over the door, and the oriel's frieze

This is piece 1 of T-1914 (S05B, the Max A. Meyer house's detailing). T-1914 was split this run. The rest of the package is in T-3365: the oriel's apron, the hoods and pendant, the north quoins, the gable's crest, the basement lights, the door's pinnacles, the stack's place, and Monroe's camera. The image gate stays on T-1914.

**What changed.** Everything here is read off the Chicagology photograph at 100 px a metre, through the existing camera.
- **Door:** the print's elliptical head (1.08 m across, springing at about 4.05 m, crown at about 4.3 m). It has a moulded stone ring and a stone pilaster each side under a capital, and one dark leaf under a two-light fanlight on a transom bar at about 3.8 m. Before, it was a square-headed brown door under a plain lintel.
- **Carved course over the door:** rings between the pilasters, 4.8–5.3 m.
- **Oriel frieze:** a carved band round the oriel under its cap (`cap_band`).
- **K01, additive:** `entrance_kit["k01.opening.door_leaf"].fanlight_transom` = `{height_m, lights, leaves}`. A flat (elliptical or segmental) door arch can now glaze its head over a plain transom bar and set its own leaf count. No other record uses it. It is held by the new `tools/test_k01_fanlight_transom.py`, which is wired into check.sh and measured in `step_isolation.json`.
- **Match record:** the door, the carved panels and the oriel frieze are now `fixed`. What is still off is written down honestly:
  - `open`: the course is laid full-width (K01 lays a carved band's course across the whole front); the pilasters have no pinnacles; the apron is plain.
  - `within tolerance`: the tracery is a plain mullion; the oriel band sits about 0.15 m high.
  - The verdict stays `differs`.
- **Liberty:** `L-k01-2009-meyer-entrance-1914` records the inventions (the ring's steps, the keystone the kit needs, the leaf's joinery and colour, and the rings standing in for foliage). It has no `Covers` line because every attribute it touches is `inferred`.

**The K01 code change and the re-emit.** `k01_frontage.py` is hashed into every K01, K12, K13 and K16 input, so editing it staled 84 assets. All 84 were re-emitted with the pure-Python emitters, and so were 85 more after merging `dev`. Every GLB except 2009's came out byte-identical, so only the manifest's input hashes moved. `validate.py --stale` reports 0 errors.

**Verification.**
- `check.sh`, all four parts green:
  - parts 1/4 and 3/4 before merging `dev`;
  - parts 2/4 and 4/4 after merging it (part 4 had first failed on the liberty's covers and the unmeasured step, both fixed; part 2 had failed on the source-use index, regenerated).
- Smoke (`--for-diff` names parts 1–15 because meshes changed): desktop stage 3, 107 passed, 0 failed; mobile stage 1, 95 passed, 0 failed.
- `photo_match.mjs` was re-rendered and the side-by-side committed.
- Not run: two of the four check parts were not re-run on the merged tree, and the smoke covered only two of its parts.

title: T-2388: the second fort's blockhouse gets the cupola its pictures draw
body:
## What

The second Fort Dearborn's blockhouse gets the cupola its own pictures draw, and loses the
invented chimney that was standing in its place. **This is a bounded partial increment of
T-2388** — the ticket's all-buildings, all-pictures acceptance is NOT met and the ticket is
released OPEN with the remaining differences recorded.

Panel 5 of the Kurz & Allison sheet of 1893, captioned "Fort Dearborn as rebuilt 1835", draws
this blockhouse with a small square body at the centre of its four-sided cap, under a little
four-sided cap of its own, and draws no stack anywhere on that roof. The two Wau-Bun
reproductions of the 1831 view (`kinzie_1857_chicago_1831_panorama`) draw the same body. That is
what is now built.

| | |
|---|---|
| before | the invented brick stack at the apex |
| after | the pictured cupola, seated into all four roof planes |

`docs/RESEARCH/second-fort-cupola-T-2388/` holds both, rendered through `photo_match.mjs` from
**one identical camera** with nothing changed between them but the blockhouse's own bytes
(`4b49f0db…` → `96d9fb80…`), beside the panel itself.

## Why, and what is and is not claimed

* **The cupola's OCCURRENCE is inferred** from the two identified pictures. Every dimension —
  the 1.8 m side, the 2.1 m body, the 0.22 m cap eave, the 36° cap pitch, the 0.12 m seat, the
  plain boarded sides with no louvres and no finial — is **reconstructed**, lives in the
  archetype rather than the record, and is admitted in `docs/LIBERTIES.md`
  § `L-second-fort-blockhouse-cupola-2388`. A tier-5 retrospective chromolithograph supplies
  form, never a metric, and its caption is not proof the feature stood on 1 July 1835.
* **`chimneys: 0` is a choice about what to DEPICT, not a finding about heating.**
  `_chimneys` stands its single stack at exactly the centre of the plan — the cupola's place —
  so the two could not both be built and one of them is pictured. The record says in as many
  words that this is not a claim of no heating, no flue, or no later secondary projection, and
  the stack has not been quietly moved somewhere else. The 1856 Kellogg/Blanchard print (filed
  misleadingly as `chicago_fort_dearborn_river_mouth_1830.jpg`) depicts about 1836–1849 and does
  show a louvred cap and an ambiguous projection beside it; that later detail is left
  unresolved, not backdated.
* **The join is real.** A box set down at the apex floats clear of the covering at its own
  corners, because the pyramid falls away in every direction — a strip of sky, and somewhere to
  hide a stack. The body's foot is carried 0.12 m below the lowest the main roof reaches
  anywhere under its footprint, so it comes up through all four planes. The main roof is the
  same four planes `_hip_roof` has always laid.

## How

* `fort_structure_params.py`: a keyword-only, **default-off** `cupola` field (added to
  `CONSUMED`, read by `from_phase`), its five reconstructed dimensions as named module
  constants, and validation that accepts **only the combination that is built** — a
  `blockhouse`, a `pyramid` roof, and no separately generated centre stack — with every
  dimension bounded and checked finite. Existing records and callers keep exactly their previous
  semantics; nothing is turned on globally.
* `fort_structure.py`: a local `_cupola` helper, called from `_building` only when the record
  asks. **Not** the lighthouse's `lantern` (only `_tower` consumes that, so setting it on a
  blockhouse would add nothing at all), not routed through the tower builder, no shared geometry
  changed. `_hip_roof`'s own overhang is now a named constant so `_cupola` reads it instead of
  copying the literal.
* `data/structures/fort_dearborn_blockhouse.json`: `form.cupola` (inferred, with its sources and
  reasoning), `form.chimneys` 1 → 0 with the full admission, and the `roof_type` note corrected —
  it used to end "no cupola is built here".
* The record keeps the `fort_structure(kind=blockhouse)` / `log_1816` phase, the surveyed seat
  and 8° rotation, the inferred 14.52 × 9.80 m footprint **and its ±25 % ambiguity**, the 5.2 m
  reconstructed walls, two storeys, the 0.45 m jetty, loopholes, doors, main pyramid at 30° and
  every palette.

## The 25-master family

Changing the producer stales every `fort_structure` asset, so **all 25 current masters** — the
already accepted 1832 lighthouse and the Lake House construction shell included — were genuinely
rebuilt on pinned **Ubuntu 26.04 / Blender 4.5.3** in two bounded native batches before the first
source commit. All 25 `inputs_sha256` in `assets/manifest.json` are the regenerated ones.
**Exactly one master's bytes moved** — `fort_dearborn_blockhouse__log_1816.glb`,
134,632 → 133,092 — and its WEB derivative was re-encoded; the other 24 came back
byte-identical and keep their genuinely bound existing derivatives. No foreign registry row was
touched, and no other job's source, claims or branches were gone near.

## The picture on the card

`kurz_allison_1893` is cited by the record, which is what puts it on the Images tab through
`compile_pictures.py`. `data/structure_grades.json` carries an explicit **pictured ruling**
saying why panel 5 is a reasonable whole picture of this named building, so the sidecar grade
derives `attested` from the rule — not hand-typed, and **not** taken as a camera-fit shortcut:
the only camera on this panel is the T-3040 compound diagnostic, whose eye reached its imposed
100 m bound, and the ruling says so.

## Verification

* `tools/check.sh --part 1/4`, `2/4`, `3/4`, `4/4` — **all four PASS**, every one a bounded
  foreground run (part 1 re-run after `compile_source_use.py` rebuilt its backlinks). No gate
  step reported a missing module.
* `tools/compile_liberties.py`, `tools/compile_scene.py --all`, `tools/compile_source_use.py`,
  `tools/changelog-entries.mjs --check`, `tools/publish.sh` — all clean.
* Before/after compound comparison through `photo_match.mjs`, same camera, both committed.
* Smoke: the parts `tools/smoke_budget.mjs --for-diff` names for this diff, at **1280×800 and
  390×780**, reported in a comment below.

## What is NOT claimed

The view's verdict is **`differs`** and `T-2388` is **released OPEN**. Still open on this
building's own picture: the camera is an unfitted 100 m diagnostic and is marked
`diagnostic_only`; the galleried range's identity, the facade openings, the other roof forms and
chimney counts, and the compound's whole composition are unresolved; and the other dated
pictures the ticket lists have not been read against the model at all. Only the roof assembly is
marked `fixed`. No new photo ticket, no split, no `done --pr`.

title: T-1909: 2000 and 2010 Prairie as whole K16 clapboard frame houses
body:
## T-1909 — Refine 2000 and 2010 detached frame houses

**Visible:** both district drafts at 2000 and 2010 Prairie now stand as whole K16 clapboard frame houses (three storeys, cased sash, bracketed eaves under low hips, canted bays, side rooms and ranges, porch across the front, flagged front walk). Shots: `docs/RESEARCH/k16-2000-2010-frame-1909/after-desktop-*.jpg`.

### What
- `house_2000_prairie`, `house_2010_prairie` move `prairie_draft` → `k16_timber` in place under the draft's own ids (phase `as_mapped_1904`; draft GLBs and their manifest entries removed).
- I read the outlines off the 1911 sheet 35 raster at full size, through the T-1250 fit: main body, '3BB' front block, '2' north range, canted bays on both flanks, the south room + canted end, and the rear south room ('2BB' at 2000) or range ('1' at 2010). The draft's 5.5 m-wide fit had stopped on the interior dashed lines. Readings table in the README.
- Kit: `host_block` lets a frame house's porch or bay name the block it stands on (until now it was always the first block). The 7 K16 houses already standing re-emit **byte-identical**.
- `tools/draft_prairie_1904.py`: a house refined off a shared lot (2000/2010/2018 share `prairie_2000`) still names its frontage's stable. Without this, the alley drafts lost their names when the house was skipped.
- Liberty `L-k16-2000-2010-frame-1909`. The draft liberty `L-draft-prairie-20-22-west-2351` is retired in part. Also re-derived: front yards replanted, walk joins re-laid, built-so-far walk, jaunt catalog, source-use backlinks, sidecars.
- No picture of either house is known (library + data/sources searched by address), so the image gate does not apply. All elevations are reconstructed.

### Not built (recorded in the liberty)
- The porches' south returns, because the kit's porch runs along one wall only.
- 2000's 0.75 m brick strip on the rear wall.
- 2010's 0.65 m rear step.

### Verification
- `check.sh --part 4/4`: **PASS** (final tree).
- `--part 1/4`: one red (`measure_generator_half` asset count, from stale draft manifest entries). Fixed, and that gate re-run green.
- `--part 2/4`: front-yard clearance, house walks and walk joins were red. Each is fixed and its own `--check` re-run green.
- `--part 3/4`: the jaunt catalog was stale. Recompiled, and `compile_jaunts --check` is green.
- Parts 1–3 were **not re-run whole** after those fixes, because of this run's clock. CI's whole gate on this PR is the referee, and `pr-automerge` merges only on green.
- `validate.py --stale`: PASS, 0 stale.
- Browser (`tools/qa_k16_t1909.mjs`, published /1904/ app, desktop): only the front and north-oblique stands were captured before the 10-min software-GL ceiling. Rear, roof and mobile stands were not taken, and the `smoke_budget --for-diff` legs were not run.

title: T-3041: the first fort's north-east small house gets its pyramid roof
body:
## What

The first fort's north-east small house carries the four-sided pyramid cap the Currey 1912 bird's-eye draws in that angle, instead of a gable. **T-3041 is a partial increment and stays OPEN** — one of the thirteen differences on that picture moves; the view's verdict is still `differs`.

`first_fort_dearborn_small_house_ne.first_fort_1803.form.roof_type`: `gable`/`reconstructed` → `pyramid`/`inferred`, cited to `currey_1912_first_fort_birdseye` and to Whistler's 1808 draught (which identifies the building, his index no. 16, and is silent about its roof).

## Why

Owner ruling of 2026-11-03 (T-3335), recorded on T-3041: of the Currey plate's departures from Whistler, adopt the blockhouse cupolas, the magazine's vault, **this house's pyramid roof** and the western gate, and keep Whistler's measured plan for everything else. This PR builds the third of those four and nothing else.

The plate was opened and read directly before any edit: at the north-east inner angle it draws a point apex, two hips to the eave corners and no ridge, with only the cap clearing the picket row. So the drawing supplies the roof's **topology and nothing else** — it is a 1912 retrospective after an 1899 sketch of an 1898 model, its camera here is `diagnostic_only`, and it is not metric. The 34° pitch stays **reconstructed**, the footprint stays the register's half-measured 12.2 × 10.0 ft, the 2.4 m wall stays unattested, and the surveyed seat, bearing and 75 ft staff are untouched. None of them was moved to fit the plate.

## How

An **opt-in `pyramid` branch** in `outbuilding.py` / `outbuilding_params.py`, never defaulted (`default_roof_type` still answers gable or shed only).

- `roof_run_m` already reads half the **short** span, so `roof_rise_m` (1.0286 m) and `apex_z_m` (3.4286 m) are right for a rectangular pyramid with **no new equation** — audited, not invented.
- `_top_z` returns a level wall head on every elevation; `_top_break` already returned `None`.
- A **triangular covering** was needed: `_roof_plane` sorts a quad into two low and two high corners and walks off the end of a triangle. `_pyramid_face` lays the same jittered boards up the slope and cuts each at the hip, so they tile the face exactly — no pile of them at the apex, no bare wedge beside each hip — and the board the apex stands over is emitted as two quads so the point is not cut off.
- **The eave is the footprint scaled about its centre, not grown by a constant margin.** `fort_structure._hip_roof` does the latter, correctly, over the square plans it serves; on this 3.72 × 3.05 m rectangle it would leave the two long walls standing **23 mm** through their own roof, because the long-span faces must be shallower to reach the same apex. Scaling instead makes all four planes pass through the wall head **exactly — measured 0.000 m** — at the price of an overhang of 0.258 m across the long span against 0.212 m across the short one. This archetype's standing promise is that `_top_z` and the roof agree exactly, so exactness won; the asymmetry is recorded as a liberty.
- A pyramid with an **open side, a loft or a chimney is refused** with a reason, rather than approximated by borrowing machinery that means something else. Every gable and shed path is unchanged, as are this building's walls, materials, 0.86 × 1.88 m batten front door and rear vent.

## The 243-asset cost, and what it actually moved

`outbuilding.py`'s bytes are hashed into every outbuilding's mesh inputs, so one branch stales **all 243 committed outbuilding masters**. Every one was regenerated on the pinned, **sha256-verified** Blender 4.5.3 (`generators/blender.pin`) on Ubuntu 26.04 **before the first source commit**, in bounded foreground batches:

| | |
|---|---|
| masters regenerated | 243 (22.5 s, one Blender start-up) |
| bytes moved | **180** — sub-millimetre float noise from different hardware, not moved geometry |
| byte-identical | 63 |
| web derivatives re-encoded | 180, in two batches of 90 (173 s + 166 s) |
| web derivatives that **changed** | **1** — this house's; the quantised derivatives absorb the noise |

No freshness hash was predicted or written by hand. `validate.py`'s staleness gate reports **1034 assets match their inputs, 0 stale**. No foreign registry row was touched, and nothing of the frame_dwelling/Jail work was modified.

## Verification

Run here, in the foreground, each inside the 600 s cap:

- `./tools/check.sh --part 1/4` → **PASS**, 287 steps (423 s)
- `./tools/check.sh --part 2/4` → **PASS**, 287 steps (343 s)
- `./tools/check.sh --part 3/4` → **PASS**, 288 steps (383 s)
- `./tools/check.sh --part 4/4` → one red, `dataset (…)`: L370 and the new entry both claimed a `roof_type` that is no longer invented. Both registers were corrected (L370 stops claiming it; the new entry supersedes L370 for this one value and covers the pitch alone) and **`python3 tools/validate.py` — the step that was red — re-ran green on the final tree: `PASS 0 error(s)`.**
- `node tools/changelog-entries.mjs --check` → OK; `tools/compile_liberties.py --check` → OK; `tools/compile_source_use.py --check` → OK.
- Before/after compound renders through `tools/photo_match.mjs` on the existing 14-member Currey camera (`first_fort_dearborn_pickets_outer`, scene 1812), **inspected directly**: the ridge that used to cross that angle is gone and the cap converges to a point. The group hash was invalidated by the peer GLB and the match record was regenerated and rebound.

**Stated plainly:** parts 3/4 and 4/4 were **not re-run whole** after that last liberties-register edit — the clock ran out — so the authoritative whole-gate run is this PR's own CI, which runs `check.sh` entire. The fifteen-case smoke was not re-run and is not claimed. Do not read this as a whole-gate pass taken here.

## Scope — what is NOT done

T-3041 and its parent T-2387 are **not finished** and T-3041 is released OPEN. Still `open` on the match record: the blockhouse cupolas, the magazine's barrel vault, the western gateway. The full first-fort acceptance — 21 named records, nine context records, every listed picture — is untouched by this increment. The NE house was **not** added to the picture's `card_members`: that would read as the 1912 retrospective attesting the building, which it cannot do, and it is explicitly optional.

Registers updated in this PR: `docs/LIBERTIES.md` (new entry + L370 narrowed), `docs/STATUS.md`, `docs/ROADMAP.md` (reasoning archive), `changelog.d/T-3041.json`.

title: T-2376: the Green Tree shoulder light gets its pointed gable cap
body:
## What

One bounded, data-only trial inside the still-open original picture case **T-2376**
(*Match the Green Tree Tavern to its pictures*). The only geometric data change is

```
phases.frame_1833.form.enclosed_left_annex.value.shoulder.front_gable_peak_m
  4.50 m  ->  4.85 m
```

so the small front-gable light over the Green Tree's enclosed shoulder reads as the
sharply pointed cap Andreas's detailed retrospective engraving draws, instead of the
blunt, nearly flat one the earlier value produced.

## Why

The builder sets the dormer wall head from the light itself (3.35 m sill + 0.70 m
height + 0.15 m head margin = 4.20 m) over a roof half-span of (0.65 m light + 0.50 m
cheeks + 0.10 m overhang) / 2 = 0.625 m. A 4.50 m peak over that is a cap of about
**25.6°**; 4.85 m gives about **46.1°** and the pointed shape the picture shows. The
clapboard courses step up the little gable face with it.

**4.85 m is a RECONSTRUCTED working control for the drawn shape, not a measurement.**
The plate carries no scale, no dimension, no geographic camera and no date, so nothing
here is measured and nothing is dated. Confidence on `enclosed_left_annex` stays
`reconstructed`; recorded in `docs/LIBERTIES.md`
§ `L-green-tree-shoulder-dormer-cap-2376`.

## The build

Built on the pinned Blender 4.5.3 (`generators/blender.pin`, sha-verified cache), never
hand-edited. `validate.py --stale` named exactly one stale master and exactly one was
rebuilt:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| inputs_sha256 | `80d47de6a302…` | `bb16568756e3…` |
| MASTER `assets/gltf/green_tree_tavern__frame_1833.glb` | `0b53a6fe…` (269,880 B) | `f213818f…` (270,816 B) |
| WEB `assets/web/green_tree_tavern__frame_1833.glb` | `0154cfad…` (48,648 B) | `65863b3c…` (48,772 B) |

The WEB derivative was encoded in the same run from the new master; the old one is not
relabelled. Every other row of `assets/manifest.json` and `assets/manifest.web.json` is
untouched, and no foreign registry entry or producer family is involved — the three
active jobs (Jail/`frame_dwelling`, first fort/`outbuilding`, second fort/`fort_structure`)
are not touched. No producer, parameter-validator, schema or recipe-scheme was edited.

### Containment, measured on the exported meshes

- triangles **3,318 → 3,330** (+12)
- the two dormer **ridge vertices raised 0.35 m** (y 4.50 → 4.85 at x 9.42, z −12.71 / −11.71)
- **24 cladding vertices added** in the 4.307–4.581 m band — the gable-course infill
- **every other primitive byte-identical** (occupied rings, door faces, ground, entry,
  main block, chimneys, glass elsewhere)
- **full model bounding box exactly equal**: `[-0.25, 0.0, -15.131628] … [18.177464, 8.722019, 0.355]`
- the peak stays below the unchanged 5.0 m main-block wall head and far below the model's
  existing 8.722 m maximum

## Before / after

Controlled: the **same camera** (`9439f5f7…`) and the **same picture** (`bfaa184f…`),
only the master rebuilt.

- before — `docs/RESEARCH/green-tree-annex-T-2376/andreas_1838-side-by-side-before-dormer-cap-20261104.jpg` (preserved by this PR)
- after — `docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/green_tree_tavern/andreas_1838-side-by-side.jpg`

The side-by-side was reviewed directly. The sharper cap reads as the pictured pointed
light; no sky seam, hole or roof penetration appears. The closed shoulder, its lower
sash and upper light, and the two separate uncovered farm wagons are retained — no
shed, posts or covered wagon returns.

## What this does NOT claim

`data/reference_views/green_tree_tavern/andreas_1838.match.json` stays **`differs`**.
The old compound OPEN row is split truthfully: only the sharper dormer cap is marked
`fixed`; a row stays **OPEN** for the shoulder's own roof slope and eaves line and for
the relative proportions of shoulder, connector and turned range against the main block.

- Trowbridge/Gale 1902 (retrospectively captioned 1835) shows an **open** post-and-roof
  wagon bay against the chosen enclosed shoulder. That source disagreement and the
  unknown conversion date remain explicit; nothing here dates the change to 1 July 1835.
- Andreas is verified public-domain **1884** and retrospective; the familiar
  "INN–1838" caption is not an independently established date, dimension or camera.
- The upper/attic opening-count disagreement between the drawings and the retained
  camera/pixel residuals stay **within tolerance** (T-3153). No new calibration barrier
  and no photo follow-up ticket.
- `chm_green_tree_1859` stays unverified / `check_required` / link-only: no derivative
  retrieved, no geometry derived, no spot. All four credited picture rows are preserved.
- The original's wider coverage — Andreas 1884, Trowbridge/Gale 1902, CHM c1859, Kurz &
  Allison 1893, plus both named reproductions — is **still incomplete**. **T-2376 stays
  open / partial / differs**; no signoff, no `done --anyway`, no split, no new ticket.

## Verification

- `./tools/check.sh --part 1/4` … `4/4`, each a bounded foreground call: **all four PASS**,
  0 red of 287 / 287 / 288 / 286 steps. No step reported a missing module, so none was
  skipped. (Part 3 first failed on `data/liberties.json` not matching the appended
  `LIBERTIES.md`; `tools/compile_liberties.py` was re-run and part 3 re-run green. Parts
  1, 2 and 4 ran before that regeneration — the hosted gate re-proves the whole tree on
  this head.)
- `tools/bake.sh --only green_tree_tavern` on the pinned Blender; master + web derivative
  written by that run.
- `node tools/photo_match.mjs data/reference_views/green_tree_tavern/andreas_1838.json`
  at the unchanged camera and picture.
- Smoke by parts per `node tools/smoke_budget.mjs --for-diff`, plus desktop 1280×800 and
  phone 390×780 review of the building in the published app — recorded in a comment below.

## Docs

`docs/LIBERTIES.md` (new bounded entry, appended — the book is not replaced),
`data/liberties.json` recompiled, `docs/STATUS.md` and
`docs/RESEARCH/green-tree-annex-T-2376/README.md` appended without replacing any
existing section, and one visitor-facing What's-New entry in `changelog.d/T-2376.json`.

title: T-2380: the log jail's keeper house, continuous palisade front and low gate
body:
## T-2380 — the log jail's keeper house, continuous palisade front and low gate

A **partial** increment on the original picture-match ticket. **The match is not
claimed and T-2380 stays open**: both reference views were re-rendered against
this geometry and both record verdict `differs`, with the remaining differences
written down.

### What ships

- **`log_jail_keeper_house`** — John Beach's house, the one Gale 1902 p51 puts
  partly inside the jail enclosure facing Randolph. Built on a new **opt-in**
  `keeper_gale_1902` layout of the native `frame_dwelling` archetype: the
  pictured W/W/D front stations, two east-gable ground sash, a small loft light
  and the stack at the pictured gable end.
- **The compound** — the palisade now runs continuously across the front, and a
  low framed, braced, hung gate (`log_jail_keeper_link`) stands on the house
  side.
- **The core is untouched.** `log_jail` keeps its mesh and its 12° roof; only its
  explicitly reconstructed access setback moves 1.30 m south, inside the ~20 m
  site uncertainty its own record declares.

### Provenance

Everything numeric here is reconstruction and says so. One new liberty,
`L-log-jail-keeper-compound-2380`, covers the footprint, position, documented
range, picture layout, construction, stories, wall height, roof pitch, plan,
paint, glazing, shutters, porch and the simplified cladding; `L148` picks up the
dealt siding stock and `L263`'s population count moves 691 → 692. The house is
`inferred`, never `documented`: Trowbridge's plate and Gale's recollection are
tier-5, the plate is captioned **1836**, and the evidence ladder forbids a
documented value resting on tier 5 alone. Andreas draws a different elevation
and that disagreement is recorded rather than reconciled. Nothing backdates the
fall-1835 court-house into the 1 July scene, and the roof is entered in the
physical-roof reconciliation as `inventory_eligible: false` — it stands in the
scene and not in the 1835 count.

### Native outputs — built here, on the pinned Blender

Not carried in from anywhere. Built on this runner on Ubuntu 26.04 with the
sha256-verified pinned **Blender 4.5.3** from `generators/blender.pin`:

- master `assets/gltf/log_jail_keeper_house__frame_1835.glb` — 70,712 bytes,
  sha256 `431dc44f37bdcb2c7f705a5b17b65fe6a1cf748d077c337b699094c9b41752a8`
- web derivative — 20,632 bytes, sha256
  `15eb2fbad5e1b8f464c30f7135297047896b4eff95f9168de6084e75e86f710e`
  (pinned gltf-transform, via `tools/web_derivatives.sh`)

**The frame family was qualified, not assumed.** The opt-in parameter refreshes
the input signature of all **271** existing `frame_dwelling` assets. All 271
were rebuilt on the pinned Blender and **every one came back byte-identical** —
the opt-in moves no vertex of any other building. Their manifest rows carry only
a new `inputs_sha256`; no asset was removed, and no foreign registry row
(including the K01 rows) was touched. An intermediate build of this very record,
before the siding deal, reproduced the earlier packet's retained master and web
pair byte-for-byte (`03aafaa4…` / `b1997083…`), which is how the pinned
toolchain was checked before anything was committed.

### The picture comparison — `differs`, with the differences named

Re-rendered with `tools/photo_match.mjs` for both views, as a group (core +
keeper) with both enclosures. Side-by-sides are in the diff at
`docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/log_jail/`. Two differences the increment **closes**
(the keeper house was absent; the compound front and gate were absent); still
open, in both views:

- the jail core reads **concealed behind the palisade**, where both pictures show
  its log walls and roof standing clear — the palisade is too high for the core
  against these pictures, or the core too low, and this increment settles
  neither;
- the compound's **relative proportions** are wrong against the plate;
- the palisade is one flat mass where both pictures draw separate boards;
- neither camera is solved — both carry `diagnostic_only: true`, so no framing
  disagreement is promoted into a metric error.

No new photo follow-up ticket is filed (T-3153). T-2380 is released back to the
queue, open, with these differences on it.

### Verification

- `tools/validate.py` — **PASS**, 0 errors (schema, provenance, liberties
  coverage, date gates, staleness: 0 stale assets).
- `./tools/check.sh --part k/4` — run in the foreground, one call each; see the
  checklist in the comments below for which parts were green at push time.
- Sidecars recompiled, `tools/rederive.mjs --check` at its fixed point, resident
  layer converged, and `tools/publish.sh` run before every gate.
- The hosted dev gate and smoke on this PR are the merge gate.

title: T-3366: 1936 Prairie's verandah takes its iron rail across the openings
body:
## T-3366 — 1936 Prairie's verandah takes the iron rail across its three openings

Piece 1 of **T-3357** (split this run; the rest is T-3367). The code comment, the record's note and the liberty cite T-3357, the ticket this was built under.

**What.** The Chicagology photograph of the Thompson/Allerton house shows a dark bar across the feet of the verandah's three arched openings (y 822 px, about 0.8 m over the floor against the openings' 45-50 px for their 1.2 m span), with a dark upright under it in the middle of the first two (x ≈ 1460 and 1527 px; the third opening is in shadow). The build had open arches with nothing in them.

- `generators/archetypes/k01_porte_cochere.py`: `corner_porch` takes an optional `rail` key `{height_m, bar_m, standards}`, validated in `_porch_rail` (0.5-1.2 m over the floor and ≥ 0.3 m under the springing; a 0.03-0.1 m bar; 0-3 standards per opening). `_dress_rail` draws a square iron bar from jamb to column across each front arch, in the middle of the wall's thickness, on evenly spaced standards.
- `data/structures/house_1918_prairie.json`: `rail: {height_m 0.8, bar_m 0.06, standards 1}`; the note says what was read and where.
- `docs/LIBERTIES.md` (+ `data/liberties.json`, recompiled): the bar's section and the standard count are reconstructed, and the iron is a reading of the dark tone (L-k01-1936-allerton-1901).
- Match record: the verandah item now records that the rail is built. It stays **open** for the verandah's place along the front, which waits on the camera re-solve (T-3367). Verdict re-reviewed: `differs`. The camera, the entrance, the stacks, the deck and the window dressings are still open.
- Rebake: `k01_emit.py` re-emitted every K01 house. Only 1936's GLB changed (+3.7 KB); the rest are byte-identical and only their input hashes were re-recorded. The 1936 web derivative was rebuilt, and the sidecars were recompiled.

**Visible?** Yes: from the street, each verandah arch now has a waist-high dark rail with a centre standard.

## Verification
- `./tools/check.sh --part k/4`, k = 1..4: all exit 0. The only numpy lines are `self-test |` lines.

- `photo_match.mjs` re-rendered the side-by-side. In the verandah crop, the rail reads as a dark bar across each opening.

title: T-1934: 1729 Prairie's stack behind the rear face, off Taylor 16554
body:
## T-1934: 1729 Prairie's stack behind the rear face, off Taylor 16554

**What.** The owner reopened T-1934 on 2026-10-28, and its image gate had two open items left, both on the house. This PR fixes the first and diagnoses the second.

1. **Fixed: the stack behind the rear face.** Taylor's no. 16554 shows a stone stack rising behind the house's rear (east) face, between its two rear dormers (x 512-523 px, cap at y 317, about 4 px over the cresting). The build had no stack there. It is now `chimneys.stacks[3]` on `pullman_house_1729_prairie` (u 1.4, v 10.0, top 18.4 m), with `L-pullman-1729-rear-stack-1934`.
   - The stack's existence, stone, size and height are read from the print. Its place on the deck is reconstructed.
   - The 16554 camera is fitted on the ground and the stable, not the house's rear: it draws the rear face about 156 px long where the print draws it about 73. So the stack is placed against the dormers instead of through the camera. It now renders between the first and second rear dormers, as the print draws it.
   - The conservatory's 16554 record now **matches**, and a `fixed` item was added to the house's own 16554 record.
2. **Diagnosed, still open: 16555's house corner, about 35 px right of the print's.** The 16555 camera fitted the wing's west end, which is the house's east wall, at u −12.12 in the conservatory frame. The 1904 scene places the house's east wall at −11.21, 0.91 m further east. The 1894 plate's record reads the same "about 1 m". The item is over the bar, so it stays `open`. The fix belongs to the house's placement or east wall (T-1881's record, where it moves every u), so this PR does not attempt it. The diagnosis is written into the record. **The ticket's image gate therefore stays open.**

**Also in this PR.** Dev's #1658 changed the shared K01 generator and rebaked only 1729 Prairie. That left 2009 Prairie (Mayer) stale by input hash, so `validate.py --all` was red on dev. 2009 Prairie is rebaked with `--only`: its mesh bytes are unchanged and the manifest's input hash is current again.

**Re-judged.** All eleven estate and house views were re-rendered on the merged house and looked at. Verdicts:
- conservatory: plate `matches`, 16554 `matches`, 16555 `differs` (the corner item)
- ranges: all three `matches`
- house: all five `differs` (T-1881's open items, unchanged)

## Verification
- `check.sh --part 1/4` through `4/4` on the pre-merge branch:
  - parts 1 and 2 were green.
  - parts 3 and 4 were red on one derived-data step each (source-use coverage, the 1904 built-so-far walk). Both were regenerated, and both steps pass when re-run.
- After merging dev and rebaking:
  - `validate.py --all` passes, with 0 errors after the Mayer restamp.
  - These also pass: `image_gate --check`, `compile_source_use --check`, `jaunt_built_so_far --check`, `compile_liberties --check` and `changelog-entries --check`.
  - The four `check.sh` parts were not re-run after the merge; CI's whole `check.sh` gates the head.
- Smoke, `--published`:
  - part 3 at mobile: 107 passed, 0 failed.
  - part 3 at desktop: 107 passed, 0 failed.
  - part 15 at desktop: cut off by the 590 s cap. Every jaunt check that ran passed with zero page errors; the one FAIL is the browser closed by the timeout. Dev's own record for this leg is also KILLED on the steward runner.
- Blender bake: `--only pullman_house_1729_prairie` and `--only mayer_house_2009_prairie`.

title: T-3088: Occupied transport loops and walk-up controls
body:
Otis Bardwell drives a reconstructed occupied wagon circuit in 1835, and Hans Johnson drives a Brougham circuit in 1904, in Full or Balanced detail. Walk up and use Interact to Stop or Continue; Step back checks visitor clearance. Driver picks and Find use the named person and vehicle’s current position. Light retires the occupied assembly and restores standing-person ownership.

Current pushed HEAD is `a6207b493f7ce06052e9e211245631a1e07f8df1`, TREE `0472b3e7d758fe265e93b2d6f508cf91564286f6`. It preserves the registered Inspector preload, driver-card data warmup, prioritized route continuations, route/model safety checks, existing provenance, standing idles and memory repairs. Latest DEV walking-path, bridge, building-dressing and changelog changes are integrated. Independent reviews preserved all owned runtime/CI files and incoming assets.

The prior whole CI gate took 29minutes and ended with one failure among 1154steps: the isolated empty-scene fixture lacked the new `draws`/card-preparation dependencies. The fixture now uses actual scene-layer bindings, retains every old assertion and tests no card/model activity for empty rows and Light. The original fixture passes in the actual app checkout.

CI now runs the existing complete native partition in eight parallel jobs. The original required check remains `gate` and succeeds only when all eight jobs succeed. Each part retains its 600second ceiling. Full history, reader/base requirements, dependencies, pool selection, event/permission/runners and changelog-entry checks are unchanged. The existing native harness passes 50checks including 14 deliberate workflow-fault refusals. This gate change unblocks this visible transport parcel; it does not reduce project coverage or quality settings.

Validation and remaining delivery work:

- Current integration passed 13 actual native/targeted commands, including transport, driven assembly, Navigator, empty scenes, native harness, report owners/checks, all-asset validation and structure clearance. All 17 owned source files match the preceding checked increment exactly.
- All five actual-HEAD changelog/identifier checks, whitespace, normal push, source guards and Git/PR readback pass. Current committed-HEAD native publication/validation and final all-asset validation pass.
- On previous 7d source, moving frames, the complete 32-check published release validation and all nine frame/memory jobs passed. The native full gate’s sole fixture failure is retained and repaired. These results are not relabelled as current-head passes.
- The previous phone world run genuinely showed Hans’s card and census within its original 30second window, with one identity. It then failed the native Find touch acknowledgement. A new observer serializes touchStart/End under the same total 30seconds, requires both acknowledgements and retains every original Find/Light predicate. Current-source world and full CI results remain pending; negative runs are preserved.

[Immutable prior checkpoint and failures](https://github.com/kevinrhaas/chicago-evidence/blob/41997711fb6d69af94e682d139f20ea8888ecb45/evidence/transport-pr1649-nav-checkpoint-7d757-2026-11-04-0000Z/MANIFEST-FINAL.json).

Merge only into DEV after current-source gates and interaction acceptance. Broader photographic appearance, anatomy, gait, boarding, riding and natural seated animation remain open. The prepared driver look-motion increment is separate. No broader ticket completion or production deployment is claimed.
